Nonlinear mixing Nonlinear mixing Ray tracer datasets Home Ray-tracer Validation The orchard scenes The forest scenes Terms of use The authors Publications Terms of use The different datasets on this website are freely available for the wider scientific community to study nonlinear mixing effects, test new unmixing methodologies, and compare its performance with other unmixing methodologies. Other applications for these datasets are strongly encouraged. The only condition attached to the use of the datasets in publications is that you refer to the original papers where these datasets are based on: The calibration of the ray-tracerand the virtual orchard: Stuckens, J., Somers, B., Delalieux, S., Verstraeten, W. W., & Coppin, P. (2009). 
     The impact of common assumptions on canopy radiative transfer simulations: A case study in Citrus orchards. Journal of Quantitative Spectroscopy and Radiative Transfer, 110(1), 1-21 . The validation of the ray-tracer to study nonlinear mixing: Somers, B., Tits, L., Coppin, P. (2014) Quantifying Nonlinear Spectral Mixing in Vegetated Areas: Computer Simulation Model Validation and First Results. IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing. To appear . For the description of the datasets: Tits, L., Somers, B., Stuckens, J., Coppin, P. (2014). Validating nonlinear mixing models: benchmark datasets from vegetated areas. 6th Workshop on Image and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing (WHISPERS). Lausanne, Switzerland, 25-27 June 2014. If you published using one of these datasets, you can always send the full reference, together with a link to an open access version of the paper, to Laurent  ( laurent.tits@biw.kuleuven.be) . It will be added to the list of publications. web development by Laurent Tits - aided by bryant smith
